$note: Every slot the three stores offer: images and text, required and optional,
including the ones this product deliberately leaves empty and the ones it
can never need. It exists because a store listing is a form with a few
dozen fields and no store tells you what you forgot — the Microsoft Store
poster art was missed exactly this way, and the omission was invisible
until someone read the upload page again.
This file is the source, not a summary. tools/check-store-images.mjs reads
the image slots, tools/check-store-listings.mjs cross-checks the text
slots against the listing files, and tools/gen-store-assets-doc.mjs renders
brand/STORE-ASSETS.md from it. A slot that is not here is not checked and
not documented, so adding one here is how a new asset enters the process.
status:    required     the store will not publish without it
recommended  accepted without it, but a surface degrades
optional     accepted without it, nothing degrades
n/a          offered by the store, impossible for this product
provided:  whether this repository currently fills the slot
kind:      copy         free text with a character limit, in a listing file
url          a link typed into the console
choice       a menu, toggle or questionnaire answer
Character limits are what the console enforces. Pixel sizes are what the
console validates at upload; none of the three resizes for you.

stores.name: Apple App Store
stores.note: iPhone only. apps/ios/project.yml sets TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY to 1, which removes every iPad and Mac slot from the form.

images.note: Ships inside the binary; App Store Connect reads it from there and offers no upload field. Generated by tools/gen-ios-appicon.mjs. An alpha channel or baked rounded corners are rejected — iOS applies its own mask.
The only screenshot size Apple requires; it downscales this set for every smaller iPhone. Captured by apps/ios/scripts/capture-store-screenshots.sh, which needs macOS.
As above, in English.
Apple derives them from the 6.9" set. Uploading them separately only creates a second set to keep in step.
iPhone-only app. The form does not ask.
Up to three 15-to-30 second videos per size, captured from a device. Not produced: the product is one screen and a verdict, and the screenshots already carry it.

images.slot: Apple Watch, Mac, Vision Pro and Apple TV screenshots
images.note: No such target in apps/ios/project.yml.
Apple requests this directly from the developer when it plans to feature an app. It is not part of a submission and there is no field for it.

text.note: Shown under the icon. Truncates on the home screen long before 30.
One line under the name, and indexed for search. Worth using.
Comma separated, 100 characters total including the commas. Never repeat a word from the name or subtitle; those are already indexed.
Above the description, and the one field that can be changed without shipping a build.
Required for every update after the first submission.
Recorded under "## App information" in the listing file.
Recorded under "## App information".
Year and legal entity. No character limit worth guarding.
"## App privacy answers" in the listing file. Must agree with Sources/QravnApp/Resources/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy or the build is rejected.
"## Review notes". A reviewer with no QR code to point a camera at is the most likely cause of a 2.1 rejection, so this field is not optional in practice.
No account, no login, no paid tier.
Apple's standard EULA applies when this is left alone.

stores.name: Google Play
stores.note: Phone form factor only. The alpha rule is the one to watch: the icon is the single Play asset allowed to carry a transparency channel.

images.note: 32-bit PNG with alpha, at most 1024 KB. Play applies its own rounded corners and shadow, so the source is a full square.
24-bit PNG or JPEG, no alpha. Play cannot publish a listing without it. Edges get cropped in some placements, so nothing load-bearing goes near them.

JPEG or 24-bit PNG, no alpha, between 320 and 3840 px per side, and the long side may not exceed twice the short side. The emulator's native 1080x2400 is 2.22 and is rejected; captures are taken after `adb shell wm size 1080x1920`.
As above, in Norwegian.
Required only for an app that declares tablet support. Becomes required the moment large-screen support is claimed.
Not distributed to TV. A TV listing needs a 1280x720 banner and at least one TV screenshot.

images.slot: Wear OS, Android Auto and XR screenshots
images.note: No such distribution. Each has its own mandatory shape and count.
A YouTube URL rather than an upload. Not produced.

text.note: The first text a customer reads, and it appears without the full description in several surfaces.
Per language, per release. Much shorter than the Apple and Microsoft equivalents, which is the usual reason a shared draft does not fit.
Play requires a contact email; the website and phone are optional.
"## Content rating questionnaire" in the listing file.
"## Data safety declaration". Must agree with the manifest: the app declares no INTERNET permission, so every collection answer is no.
Ads, target audience, news, COVID-19, data safety, government apps, financial features.
"## Store settings": app category, contact details, external marketing opt-out.

stores.name: Microsoft Store
stores.note: Submitted as a PWA. Partner Center offers the largest form of the three and almost all of it is optional, which is precisely why a written list is needed.

images.note: At least one. The store asks for 1366x768 or larger and accepts up to 3840x2160; these are rendered at 1920x1080 by tools/store-shots/capture.mjs.
As above, in Norwegian.
Partner Center falls back to the logos inside the package when these are absent. A PWA package has no good source for them, so they are supplied.

The main logo for Windows 10 and 11 customers, and required for Xbox display. Partner Center labels the slot 9:16 and then demands 720x1080 and 1440x2160, which are 2:3. Follow the pixels: a true 9:16 asset is rejected at upload.
Used across several Store layouts, and becomes the main logo when poster art is absent. Carries the wordmark, which is what separates it from the identically sized Xbox promotional square.
Top of the listing on Windows 10 1607 and later. Must not contain the product's title, and is required if a trailer is to play at the top of the listing.
Must carry the title in the top three quarters; text overlays may cover the bottom quarter.
Same title rule as the branded key art.
Must not carry the title, which is the opposite of the two Xbox slots above and the reason this is not the same file as box-art-1080x1080.png.
Uploaded video with its own thumbnail. Not produced. Super hero art is required before a trailer can head the listing.

text.note: Reserved once for the whole product; the per-locale field selects among reserved names.
Used in search results and on smaller surfaces. Far longer than the Play field of the same name.
Up to 20 bullets of 200 characters, shown as a list.

Seven terms, 30 characters each, and 21 individual words across all of them. Not shown to customers. A term made only of words already in the name or description is wasted, because those fields are indexed anyway.
Deliberately blank: this is the first submission and there is nothing to be new against.
A shorter name for tiles where the full one does not fit. The product name is 26 to 28 characters, so it already fits.
For a name that sorts badly. "QRavn" does not.
An alternate name for spoken requests.
The Standard Application License Terms apply when this is left alone.
Free text for hardware the app needs. A camera is already implied by the product.
Required for any product that connects to the network or collects anything, and Partner Center asks regardless.
"## Properties and Store settings" in the listing file.
Accessibility, notifications, hardware requirements and the rest of the Properties page.
